title: Extract a Given Number of Randomly Selected Elements From a List
required_features: Effectful stateful PRNG operations, including an exact model of per-call OCaml Random.init 0 initialization and bounded draws.
A probabilistic/effect semantics that can specify random selection rather than a pure set/length relation.
A sequence/multiset relation capable of preserving list occurrence multiplicity and constraining result order.
Additional authoritative specification of invalid n behavior and the draw algorithm/order beyond the sole official example, if exact behavior on all inputs is required.
semantic_obligations: Expose rand_select with exact interface 'a list -> int -> 'a list.
For documented valid requests, return exactly n selected occurrences and never exceed any source value's multiplicity.
Initialize Random with seed 0 at the start of each function invocation in documented reproducible mode.
Match the official exact example: rand_select ["a"; "b"; "c"; "d"; "e"; "f"; "g"; "h"] 3 = ["e"; "c"; "g"].
Do not invent behavior for negative n or n greater than the input length; the solution-free source leaves it unstated.
Do not treat a finite test run as a proof of a random or probabilistic property.

source_provenance.solution_section: One section found and quarantined before inspection; no solution bodies used.

notes: No contract.sq or synthesis invocation was produced. Calling Synquid on a set/length-only approximation would be unsound: it would omit the required Random effects and cannot determine the specified seeded output order. Independent OCaml tests are retained, with a deliberately incorrect test-only negative-control stub used to demonstrate that the semantic oracle rejects a nonconforming implementation. A candidate generated later is only a candidate until mechanical lowering plus these OCaml tests succeeds.
